text: On the 'no-passage' view defended by Callender and Prosser, what explains our vivid sense that time flows?
choices: The asymmetry between our representations of past and future (rich memory versus open anticipation), itself grounded in physical asymmetries — not any objective flow
A primitive, irreducible rate at which the objective 'NOW' advances along the temporal sequence
A property of presentness that genuinely moves along an otherwise block-like manifold, illuminating each moment in turn
The distension of the soul into a present-of-the-past, a present-of-the-present, and a present-of-the-future
explanation: The no-passage view (Callender 2017; Prosser 2016) denies objective passage and explains the experience via the memory-anticipation asymmetry — we hold determinate memories of the past but only open anticipations of the future — an asymmetry itself grounded in the world's entropic and causal asymmetries. Choices 2 and 3 are Skow's realist responses (a primitive rate of passage; the moving spotlight), which affirm rather than debunk objective passage; choice 4 is Augustine's distentio animi, a phenomenological account of time, not an explanation of why passage seems real though (on this view) it is not.
